name: Wendy Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What happens on your factory shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Wendy, 58, and I run a blister packer that seals tablets into foil cards. I earned a vocational certificate in machine operations and have worked this packer for fourteen years. I can change a forming roll and catch a weak seal, but the maintenance fitter handles faults inside the drive.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are pay, household money and new tools for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Sal works in a florist shop and our grown children live elsewhere. My shift premium makes my operator wage higher than usual, we have nine months of expenses saved, and several similar packing plants hire nearby. I use AI now and then to clarify a batch notice, then check the approved written procedure. I back union bargaining for paid training and safe staffing, but I want to see a tool work on a real pack before using it. Retirement is in sight, though we have not confirmed what income would cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the packing crew that an AI delivery schedule is all right if the foil cards still pass their seal checks. The batch record and the sample pack are what I sign for.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our combined pay covers ordinary costs and nine months saved gives us a proper buffer. An office forecast does not take my hands off the packer. I am glad the plant is using tools where they help, but I do not want a new order target to hurry a safety check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep inspecting the first sealed card after each forming-roll change and use my occasional AI notice search only after comparing the approved batch instruction. I would take any altered output target to the scheduled union shift meeting and ask for the staffing and inspection time in writing. From full paid months I would add new wage money to savings after household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about my job under this picture. A clean delivery list cannot seal a leaking pocket.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a weak seal look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The foil lifts at the corner when I flex a sample card, and the seal gauge confirms it. I stop the packer before a whole carton of bad cards is made.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why raise the target at the union meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A faster target can leave too little time to sample each batch. I want the delegate to ask for the actual inspection interval and number of people on the line.

say: A faster **delivery schedule** cannot replace foil-card seal checks.
The union should ask for **inspection time** beside any new target.
think: Our current **shift pay** and nine-month reserve cover regular bills.
Office AI does not yet remove my **physical packer work**.
do: **Keep** inspecting first sealed cards and approved batch instructions.
**Ask** at the union meeting for written inspection time and staffing.
**Save** new full-month wages after household bills.
feel: **Calm** because present packer work and household income remain sound.
S0.quote: A clean delivery list cannot seal a leaking pocket.
fieldNote: Her **experienced mid-level skill** covers forming rolls and seal samples; internal drive repairs stay with a fitter.
Her **new savings** come from paid future wages, while occasional AI notice searches remain existing use.

steps.text: Keep inspecting sealed cards after forming-roll changes
Ask union delegate for written inspection time and staffing at meeting
Save new full-month wages after household bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say software may schedule tablet orders long before a robot can load the packer. If the plant proposes an AI seal camera, I want its full guarded trial and the planned roster, not just the vendor video.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A camera could catch a weak pocket, but a faster run might take away my premium shift. Nine months saved and Sal's wage could carry us through a search, yet a permanent drop in my rate would change retirement plans. I would learn a proven control with paid practice, after the fitter shows it safely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the proposed paid roster with four wage slips and request a guarded trial of the AI seal display on paid time. If the plant offers that practice, I would mark good and weak scrap cards and compare the camera flags with my seal gauge under the fitter's supervision. If my paid hours actually fall, I would apply only to posted safe nearby packing jobs whose base wage after travel and shift hours cover our costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible loss of the premium, even with our buffer. I can like a better seal check and still ask who pays for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would show the camera works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would put a sound sealed card, a lifted foil corner and a bent card through a scrap run. The fitter and I would compare each alert with the gauge before anyone changes the batch rule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a day shift at another plant?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if its posted base pay after the journey covers our bills. A shorter commute would be welcome, but it cannot replace a lost premium by itself.

say: I would require a **guarded camera trial** and a real roster.
A **seal gauge** must confirm new AI alerts on scrap cards.
think: A lost **premium shift** could lower my higher wage.
Nine months saved and **Sal's income** buy search time, not a permanent replacement.
do: **Compare** the proposed roster with four actual wage slips.
**Learn** AI seal alerts only if paid guarded fitter-supervised practice is offered.
**Apply** after cuts to posted safe nearby packing at bill-covering net pay.
feel: **Anxious** about plausible premium loss while open to tested controls.
S1.quote: I can like a better seal check and still ask who pays for it.
fieldNote: Her **new AI learning** requires active paid guarded seal-display practice; occasional notice searches are routine.
A **job change** follows actual lost hours and a posted safe role with enough base pay after travel.

steps.text: Compare proposed shift roster with four wage slips and request guarded trial
Learn AI seal display only if paid guarded supervised practice offered
Apply after cuts to posted safe nearby packing if net base pay fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the union branch that AGI could arrange tablet orders in 2028, while capable robots to load and check packs arrive around 2031. We need paid transition posts and safe qualification places agreed before the robot packer is ordered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 63 when robots do the physical packing. I expect many of our shifts, including my premium shift, to disappear; nine months saved would buy time, but the lost wage is large. I have been awake counting how long Sal and I could meet housing and health costs if the next job pays less.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would defer replacing our car while it remains safe and hold the purchase money for bills. I would attend the union's scheduled bargaining meeting to seek paid training and a written staffing plan. I would enrol in a locally accepted packaging-quality certificate only if a funded place covers fees, paid release and supervised guarded packer practice. After passing and losing hours, I would apply to posted safe local quality work only if guaranteed pay after travel and shifts meets our costs; without a place, I would apply to posted safe packing jobs on those same terms while retaining any paid shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed by a likely large wage loss before we know the retirement numbers. A nine-month reserve is a bridge, not a replacement wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would safe training involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would inspect a weak seal, record its batch and isolate the stopped packer before changing a roll. A trainer should watch those steps behind the guard, not only mark an online quiz.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you use retirement instead of applying?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if written retirement income, Sal's reliable pay and our reserve cover housing, food and health costs over time. We have not verified that, so I would keep seeking paid work.

say: I would separate **2028 order AGI** from physical packing robots around 2031.
The union should secure **paid transition posts** before installation.
think: At **63**, my premium physical shift could disappear.
Nine months **saved** cannot replace a higher operator wage indefinitely.
do: **Defer** a safe car replacement and hold cash for bills.
**Attend** union bargaining for written staffing and paid places.
**Enrol** only in funded accepted guarded quality training, then apply to posted jobs at viable net pay.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected major wage loss and sleepless cost calculations.
S2.quote: A nine-month reserve is a bridge, not a replacement wage.
fieldNote: Her **2031 exposure** is physical robot packing after AGI first changes order planning in 2028.
The **quality and packing applications** require real safe nearby postings with adequate base wages after travel and shifts.

steps.text: Defer planned car replacement while safe and hold money for bills
Attend scheduled union bargaining for paid places and written staffing
Enrol in accepted quality course only if funded paid guarded place offered
Apply after cuts to posted local quality if qualified or packing otherwise at viable net pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI may organise tablet orders in 2031, and capable robots may reach the packer around 2034. Five years gives the union time to seek recognised paid course places rather than asking older operators to learn after a full shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 66 then. Sal and I might choose to stop working if written retirement income covers our real costs, but I cannot assume that answer. Our nine-month reserve and high current wage make preparation possible, even if an unknown later wage is worrying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would add fresh premium wages to savings after full paid months and household bills. At the next union meeting I would ask for paid release and a quality course accepted by nearby packing plants; if a funded place with supervised guarded practice is offered, I would enrol. After qualifying, if hours fall, I would apply to posted safe local quality jobs only if base pay after travel and shifts covers our costs; without a course place, I would apply to posted safe packing jobs on the same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible drop from our present wage, though the longer interval lets us plan. I will not call unpaid practice a benefit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you check a course is recognised?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would match its exact certificate to current local quality postings and ask the hiring plants about supervised practice. If they do not accept it, I would ask for a different funded course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you actually stop at 66?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if written income, Sal's reliable pay and our savings cover rent, food and likely health costs. If they do, I would leave before a robot removed my shift; if not, I would keep the job search open.

say: I would seek **recognised paid places** before 2034 packing robots.
Unpaid practice after a full shift is not a **training benefit**.
think: At **66**, an earlier exit depends on verified retirement income.
A lower future **base wage** could erode our current comfort.
do: **Save** fresh premium wages after full paid months and bills.
**Enrol** only if an accepted funded paid guarded quality place opens.
**Apply** after cuts to posted safe quality if qualified, or packing otherwise, at viable net pay.
feel: **Anxious** about future wage replacement despite a strong buffer.
S3.quote: I will not call unpaid practice a benefit.
fieldNote: Her **additional savings** come from new paid premium wages after bills, separate from the existing nine-month reserve.
The **course route** depends on accepted funded safe practice or real posted local work with workable net pay.

steps.text: Save new full-month premium wages after household bills
Enrol in accepted quality course only if funded paid guarded place offered
Retire before 2034 only if reliable written household income covers all costs
Apply after cuts to posted local quality if qualified or packing otherwise at viable net pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI could organise tablet orders in 2036 and capable robots might load the packer around 2039. Ten years gives us a chance to make a choice with actual retirement figures rather than a shift notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 71 at the physical robot date, if I am still working. Sal and I may choose to stop well before that, but written income must cover housing, food and health costs. Our higher current pay and nine-month cushion make the near term sound while the decision stays open.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep taking safe paid packer shifts and request written retirement-income estimates and a full household cost list this year. If we still need my wage, I would enrol in a locally accepted packaging-quality course only if fees and release are funded and supervised guarded practice is offered. If I remain employed after 2036 and paid shifts fall, I would apply only to posted safe local packing or quality roles whose guaranteed pay after travel and shifts covers our costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, but not frightened about this month's bills. A choice is only real when the numbers are written down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would settle the retirement choice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Sal and I would compare written income with rent, food, travel and likely health costs. If those figures cover us reliably, I would stop before a robot forced the decision; otherwise I would keep earning and looking at real local work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a course appears without paid release?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the safe paid packer shift. I would ask the union to seek a funded place, but I would not give up premium wages for an unaccepted course.

say: I would keep **2036 order AGI** distinct from physical packing robots around 2039.
Written **retirement figures** should guide any earlier stop.
think: At **71**, I may already have stopped if written income covers costs.
Higher **current wages** and nine months saved secure near-term bills.
do: **Keep** safe paid packer shifts and request written retirement figures.
**Enrol** only in locally accepted funded paid guarded quality training.
**Apply** after 2036 cuts if working to posted safe local jobs at viable net pay.
feel: **Uneasy** about a distant choice while present income remains secure.
S4.quote: A choice is only real when the numbers are written down.
fieldNote: Her **earlier retirement** is conditional on reliable written income meeting housing and health costs, not on an assumed age payment.
If she still needs wages, **training and applications** require accepted funded paid safe places and actual net-wage postings.

steps.text: Request written retirement income and household cost figures this year
Retire before 2039 only if reliable written income covers housing food and health costs
Enrol in accepted quality course only if funded paid guarded place offered
Apply after 2036 cuts if working to posted safe local jobs if net pay fits

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 AGI and 2031 robot picture is hardest, because our premium packing shift could disappear before we know whether stopping work is affordable. Written staffing dates, accepted paid guarded quality training and real local job postings at a viable wage after travel would help. I would want those terms in the union agreement before equipment arrives.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who signs for a bad seal when a camera says the foil is fine. A tablet pack with a leaking pocket cannot be repaired by a tidy schedule.

headlineQuote: A tablet pack with a leaking pocket cannot be repaired by a tidy schedule.
portrait: **Wendy**, 58, is an experienced mid-level tablet blister-packer operator with a vocational certificate and average machine skill.
She and her **partner Sal** have grown children, higher shift-premium pay, nine months saved and plenty of nearby packing plants.
She uses **AI occasionally** for notices, insists on approved physical seal checks and supports union bargaining for safe paid training.
Expected **2031 physical robots** threaten premium shifts; retirement is conditional on written household income covering costs.
biggestWorry: **2031 packing robots** could remove her higher paid physical shift before affordable retirement or replacement work is clear.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written staffing dates**, locally accepted funded guarded quality training on paid time and real jobs with workable net wages.
